headline: A loss like that follows you into ordinary life
body: Route 22 scored nearly a hundred and sixty-eight points last week and lost by less than one. A loss like that follows you into ordinary life. You’re buying toothpaste on Wednesday and suddenly remembering your tight end falling down. Now they get Skatt, who just beat Cody and Ferret—a two-man operation still looking for one win. Both teams are two and two, but Route 22 has considerably more material prepared about why. Skatt can win this matchup and make an already exhausting explanation significantly longer.

headline: The division of responsibilities
body: Cody and Ferret have demonstrated that two people can manage a fantasy team without either of them winning a game. I’m interested in the division of responsibilities. Does one select the lineup while the other explains what should have happened? Hopkins arrives in first place, an unpleasant guest at an already difficult time. If the All Ugly Team finally wins, watch how quickly shared responsibility becomes competing claims of authorship. If they lose, I imagine we’ll hear about the schedule. Neither manager, presumably, was responsible for making that.

headline: The danger of winning by less than a point
body: Kraft won by less than a point last week. That is a dangerous amount of success to give somebody, because by Friday they’ve decided it reflects their instincts. Danir is one and three despite scoring more than Kraft this season, and his opponents keep having enormous afternoons. He has a legitimate complaint, which is unfortunate, because legitimate complaints are much harder to make fun of. Kraft could show some sensitivity here. But if he wins another close one, I suspect we’re getting unsolicited advice from a man who escaped last Sunday through a bathroom window.

headline: The points column has a grievance
body: Sherm leads the league in scoring and is two and two. He put up a hundred and fifty-three last week and lost again. At this point, asking how his team’s doing requires enough time for a second answer. CeeDeep just handed Lloyd its first loss and would probably enjoy adding the league’s top scorer to the collection. This is a proper test, but Sherm needs the result more. Another impressive losing score and he’ll be sending screenshots of the points column like the rest of us haven’t learned to read.

headline: An inconvenient relationship with fairness
body: Kupp Kupp Doubs has the fewest points in the league and a three-and-one record. I would advise against asking how the season is going unless you have somewhere else to be. Roy has scored more and won less, which is precisely the sort of thing one promises not to mention, then mentions before the drinks arrive. They’re projected about a point apart this week. A Roy victory would settle a small matter of fairness. A Kupp victory would be considerably worse for everyone who has to listen to him.

headline: The cost of a second consecutive loss
body: Lloyd has suffered its first loss, which means we can retire any private thoughts about an undefeated season before they become a commemorative purchase. The team is still three and one. Baker is one and three after losing to Roy by fewer than four points, and another close defeat will do very little for his temperament. Lloyd needs to avoid turning a setback into a discussion. Baker needs a win before he starts calculating what his record would be against everybody else’s schedule. That spreadsheet has never improved a Sunday.

headline: The trouble with one victory
body: Cody has won a game, so naturally the next step is to find out whether he can be normal about it. Sandy gets the first opportunity to intervene. ZAYWATCH is favored, although I wouldn’t recommend explaining that to Cody too extensively before Sunday. A man who has just escaped oh and four is very receptive to the idea that nobody believed in him. If Sandy wins, order is restored. If Cody wins, we may discover that one and three was merely the opening chapter of a story he intends to tell at considerable length.

headline: An injustice that a win cannot settle
body: Andrew and Patrick are both one and three, but Andrew has scored more than a hundred and thirty points more. I bring this up because Patrick’s team is called A Cautionary Tale, and the caution appears to be that you can do substantially less work and end up beside Andrew anyway. They meet this week to settle absolutely none of the larger injustice. If Patrick wins, Andrew will have enough evidence to ruin a perfectly good dinner. If Andrew wins, he’ll still want to walk everyone through the evidence. I would let him order first.

headline: Somebody has to beat Greg
body: Greg is four and oh. Until someone beats him, everyone else has to tolerate whatever confidence comes with that. Paul gets the next attempt, and he’s a credible one: Croatian Sensation has actually outscored Greg across the season. Of course, pointing that out before winning is how you end up receiving a screenshot of the standings with no accompanying text. Paul can spare the league another week of unbeaten Greg. He just has to finish the job before Greg starts describing his lineup decisions as a philosophy.

headline: The price of looking down the standings
body: Matt has two wins. Joe has one. Their season scoring is almost identical, so Matt should enjoy the distinction while it remains available. Joe finally won last week and now gets a chance to catch him directly. There’s a particular irritation in losing to someone you’ve been looking down on in the standings: suddenly you’re level, and he wants to discuss momentum. Matt can prevent that conversation by winning. Joe can make it unbearable by winning comfortably. Neither outcome requires a speech, although I doubt that will stop the beneficiary.

headline: A victory lap through a populated area
body: Ravi scored a hundred and sixty-eight last week, an amount that can make a person start answering questions nobody asked him. Nipun has just suffered his first loss, so I imagine he’s especially available for that energy. Both are three and one. This is a wonderful opportunity for Nipun to stop Ravi’s victory lap while it’s still passing through a populated area. Ravi, meanwhile, can win and spend another week being technically entitled to the attitude. The rest of the league should be rooting for a deeply humbling ninety-eight to ninety-seven.

headline: A compelling case against the standings
body: Scrump leads the league in scoring and has one win. Ordinarily I dislike hearing a man explain why his record is misleading, but in this case I’m prepared to remain seated. Runit arrives at three and one, fresh off a huge week, carrying the cheerful confidence of someone whose points have actually been accepted as payment. Scrump needs this win before the injustice becomes his entire personality. Runit can afford to lose. I wouldn’t say that to him, but I would enjoy watching someone else try.

headline: Two and two, with different ideas about the future
body: Alan beat Andrew by sixty-eight last week. That’s enough to make this week’s opponent start checking his lineup on a Thursday morning. Cody also comes off a strong win, but Alan has been scoring more consistently across the season. Both are two and two, so somebody gets to leave the middle of the pack and act like he always belonged elsewhere. Cody needs to make Alan work for it. Another comfortable win and Alan may start treating lineup questions from friends as requests for professional consultation.

headline: The thank-you note remains missing
body: RFK Jr’s Bears gave Mohsin his first win last week. I’d like to know whether there was a thank-you note, or whether everyone agreed to handle it discreetly. Corey also lost, which brings us to two men at two and two who would very much like to discuss something else. Conveniently, they can play each other. The winner gets to say he’s back. Back from where is unclear; neither has gone anywhere yet. The loser gets another week of opening the app, looking briefly, and closing it a little harder than necessary.

headline: An unreasonable public position
body: Andrew lost by sixty-eight last week, a result large enough that checking the app again begins to feel like a personal choice. Now he faces Sandy, who also lost but can at least discuss his afternoon without lowering his voice. Both are two and two. I’m curious how much confidence Andrew can recover before kickoff, because the name Jerruh’s World does rather obligate him to maintain an unreasonable public position. Sandy has a chance to keep the crisis going. Another ninety-point performance and I’d expect Andrew to express full confidence in himself.

headline: Let the result arrive before the statement
body: Patrick finally won, scored a hundred and forty-three, and now has the league’s strongest projection. You can see how a man might become difficult to sit beside. Bennett is three and one after losing by fewer than three points, so he’s unlikely to appreciate a recovery story unfolding at his expense. Patrick needs a second win before declaring anything fixed. Bennett needs to remind him why there are still two wins between them. This is an excellent week to let the result arrive before issuing a statement about the direction of the franchise.

headline: The statistical explanation will be awkward
body: Pete has scored about seventy-six more points than Bryan. They have the same record, which I suspect Bryan finds easier to accept. Bryan won last week; Pete lost to Cody, so they also arrive with different appetites for conversation. A Bryan victory would make the statistical explanation rather awkward for Pete to continue offering. A Pete victory would allow him to behave as though the matter had always been obvious. There is very little room here for a gracious winner. Fortunately, neither man has been asked to prepare remarks in advance.

headline: The game drops a piano on you
body: Mohsin finally got his first win, and immediately the league sends him Ordway and Son. You finish the tutorial and the game drops a piano on you. Ordway is in first place after escaping Bennett by fewer than three points, so he should understand that survival doesn’t always need to look impressive. Mohsin has an opportunity to become everyone’s favorite person for about twenty minutes by beating the leader. Ordway just needs to avoid becoming the second chapter of a comeback story told by a man who was oh and three a week ago.
